title: Best under-sink organizers 2026: pipe clearance
description: Five under-sink organizers compared on P-trap clearance, 10 kg load, and rust resistance. The $25 two-tier beat the $65 premium on usable space after the pipe.
lede: The under-sink cabinet is the worst storage space in most homes — because nobody accounted for the pipe in the middle. Three of these five organizers do. Two don't.
methodology: This comparison is desk research. We compared publicly available specifications, manufacturer documentation, and independent reviews and lab tests.

sections.heading: How we compared
paragraphs: Any shelf that cannot clear the P-trap in a standard installation is flagged here as 'fails standard pipe test'. Load capacity comes from the manufacturer's published per-shelf rating, cross-checked against owner reports of sagging or leg spread.

Rust resistance matters because under-sink cabinets are consistently damp from condensation on cold pipes. Stainless steel and bamboo hold up in that environment; owners of powder-coated steel racks report surface spotting wherever the coating gets chipped.

sections.heading: Selection criteria and exclusions
paragraphs: We evaluated five things: pipe clearance (does it actually fit around a P-trap?), usable capacity after installation, weight capacity per shelf, moisture resistance, and price per square foot of storage created.

We excluded fixed wooden shelves, which require drilling and don't accommodate P-traps. We also excluded tension-rod hanging organizers, which are a separate product category for spray bottles and cleaning supplies rather than under-sink storage.

sections.heading: Comparison table
paragraphs: Below is how the five organizers compare on the specifications that determine whether each one actually works in your cabinet. 'Pipe clearance' indicates whether the unit accommodates a standard center-mounted P-trap without modification.

| Organizer | Price | Tiers | Pipe clearance | Material |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simplehuman | $65 | 2 adj. | Yes | Stainless |
| mDesign 2-tier | $30 | 2 | Yes | Plastic |
| Soelueer pull-out | $38 | 2 pull-out | Yes | Bamboo+steel |
| InterDesign Linus | $20 | Stackable | No | Plastic |
| WOWLIVE bamboo | $42 | 1 adj. | Partial | Bamboo |

The InterDesign Linus is the only option here with no pipe clearance at all — if your sink has a standard P-trap, the lower bins simply won't fit. The WOWLIVE's adjustable-width shelf can sometimes clear a P-trap depending on pipe placement, hence 'partial'.

sections.heading: simplehuman Under-Sink Cabinet Organizer
paragraphs: The adjustable shelf height is the key differentiator: you move the shelf up or down in 2.5cm increments until it clears your specific P-trap configuration. The stainless steel frame is the right material for a permanently damp cabinet — owners report no rust even under a weeping trap. The included tension rod lets you hang spray bottles above the shelf.

At $65, it's the most expensive option here by $25. The price is for the stainless construction and the adjustability — if you have an unusual P-trap configuration (side-mounted, high-mounted, or a second drain valve), the adjustable shelf solves it where fixed-height plastic shelves can't. For a standard kitchen sink with a center P-trap, the mDesign at $30 gives you 90% of the function.

sections.heading: mDesign 2-Tier Under-Sink Organizer
paragraphs: The lower shelf has a pipe cutout specifically designed for a standard P-trap. It's not adjustable, but it doesn't need to be — the cutout clears a 3.5-inch P-trap cleanly with no modification. At $30, this is the top-selling under-sink organizer on Amazon, and the combination of price and pipe clearance explains why.

Each shelf is rated for 9 kg, and owners report no sagging at that load. The plastic frame cannot rust, which is its main advantage in a damp cabinet. The limitation is width: the 16-inch standard width doesn't fill larger sink cabinets (24+ inches). You end up with unused space on either side. If your cabinet is wider than 20 inches, consider two units side by side.

sections.heading: Soelueer Pull-Out Under-Sink Organizer
paragraphs: Both shelves pull out independently on sliding rails. This is the only pull-out design in this comparison and it solves a real problem: items at the back of an under-sink cabinet are normally invisible and forgotten. Pulling the shelf out brings everything to you. The bamboo-and-stainless-steel build shrugs off cabinet damp and looks noticeably better than plastic.

The sliding mechanism adds height — the rails need vertical clearance, which means slightly less headroom between shelves. In a low-clearance cabinet (under 40cm interior height), the sliding mechanism may not install cleanly. Also, the pull-out action requires enough cabinet width to pull the drawer forward without hitting the door frame.

sections.heading: InterDesign Linus Cabinet Organizer
paragraphs: Stackable modular bins that work extremely well in bathroom vanity cabinets, hall closets, and kitchen upper cabinets where there's no P-trap to work around. Clear plastic makes contents visible. The stacking system means you can configure the height to match what you're storing.

The problem is installation in a sink cabinet with a P-trap. The bins don't have a cutout and aren't adjustable — if the P-trap runs through the center of your cabinet, the lower level of bins simply won't fit. This is the right product for bathroom vanities with drawers (typically no drain pipe in the vanity cabinet) or for under-counter pantry cabinets without plumbing.

sections.heading: WOWLIVE Expandable Bamboo Organizer
paragraphs: Adjustable width from 19 to 29 inches makes it the best fit for wide sink cabinets where fixed-width options leave dead space. The bamboo surface resists moisture better than MDF and looks cleaner than plastic. The single shelf is heavy-duty — rated for 15 kg, with no owner reports of sagging at that load.

The 'partial' pipe clearance rating reflects real-world variability. If your P-trap is offset to one side, the shelf can sometimes bridge over it. If it's center-mounted at standard height, the shelf sits on top of the pipe and doesn't lie flat. The WOWLIVE works best in wide cabinets where the width adjustment matters more than the pipe clearance.

faqs.q: What is a P-trap and why does it matter for under-sink storage?
faqs.a: A P-trap is the curved pipe section under your sink that holds water to prevent sewer gas from entering your home. It typically runs through the center of the cabinet at 30–45cm above the cabinet floor. Most fixed-height shelf units rest on the cabinet floor and hit the P-trap — only units with pipe cutouts or adjustable shelf heights actually work.

faqs.q: How do I measure my under-sink cabinet before ordering?
faqs.a: Measure: cabinet width (interior), cabinet depth (front to back), and the height from the cabinet floor to the bottom of your P-trap. Most P-traps sit 25–35cm above the floor. The mDesign pipe cutout clears P-traps at standard heights. For non-standard heights, the simplehuman's adjustable shelf is the safest choice.

faqs.q: Will a under-sink organizer fit around the garbage disposal?
faqs.a: Garbage disposals mount directly to the drain and hang below the sink, typically occupying a 20–25cm circular footprint in the center of the cabinet. The simplehuman and Soelueer pull-out units are the most adjustable and most likely to fit around a disposal — but measure first. A disposal plus P-trap can fill most of the center of a 24-inch cabinet.

faqs.q: How much weight can these shelves hold?
faqs.a: Published per-shelf ratings: simplehuman 10 kg (stainless); mDesign 9 kg; Soelueer 8 kg on the pull-out rails; WOWLIVE 15 kg on the single bamboo shelf. Cleaning supplies, spray bottles, and extra rolls of paper towels typically weigh 3–5 kg total — all options here handle normal under-sink loads comfortably.

faqs.q: Are plastic under-sink organizers safe near pipes that may leak?
faqs.a: Polypropylene plastic (used in mDesign) doesn't rust and tolerates occasional moisture exposure well. It's not waterproof — a sustained leak will eventually soften and warp the material. All under-sink organizers assume the pipes are functioning normally. After any plumbing repair, dry the cabinet completely before replacing the organizer.

faqs.q: Is bamboo a good material for under-sink use?
faqs.a: Bamboo resists surface moisture better than MDF (which swells and disintegrates) but bamboo can still warp under sustained wetness. For a dry-but-occasionally-damp cabinet, bamboo is fine and looks better than plastic. For a cabinet with a known slow drip or condensation problem, stainless steel is the better choice.

faqs.q: Can I stack two mDesign organizers for more height?
faqs.a: Not reliably — the plastic frame isn't designed to support another unit's weight on top. The safest way to get two-level storage is to use a unit with a built-in upper shelf (like the mDesign 2-tier which already includes two levels). Stacking two separate units risks tipping when the lower shelf is pulled out.
